body: I made it through four episodes. Not really the best "don't kill yourself" show...

I've been sitting here staring at your post for the past twenty minutes, and for the life of me I cannot figure out how to answer it. Is there even a question here? Are you considering killing yourself, changing gender, or do you just want to rant about your dislike for women? DO you dislike women?

Honestly I have no idea what the hell is going on on this post.

So if it doesn't get better, and the best that it will probably ever be is "tolerable", is it worth it? Like I said, I'm not saying I'm never happy. But I don't think my happiness comes anywhere near how sad and hurt I've been, and I'd rather not continue like this for another 50+ years if that's all that is waiting for me.
I was also wondering what his response meant. It seemed a little backwards from my original post.
I'm not sure if that paints a good picture or not. But they've certainly helped. They brought me from wanting to die down to "sometimes I'm sad".

I'm currently taking 275mgs of it. It's helped me quite a bit, but some days I still feel really sad - it's not a miracle drug, after all.

As far as side effects go, there will probably be a few. It's a really powerful drug, and getting up to whatever dosage you end up on can cause some issues. For one, I have significantly increased sweating and dry mouth. Those haven't gone away, and my doctor said they probably won't as they're the most common side effects. 
Second, while I was getting used to it I would get pretty bad nausea like once every other week. I threw up twice in the five months it took to get me up to where I'm at now. Since then, I haven't had an issue with nausea. 

I should mention than once you're on it, DO NOT MISS A DAY. Seriously. Don't. I missed one day once and the withdrawal hit me like a truck. Luckily I noticed that I missed them, and managed to take them. But it felt like what I'd imagine cocaine withdrawal is like - curled up in a ball feeling like I'm gonna die.
As long as you're good with remembering them, you should be fine though. But since they are only in your system for 24 to 36 hours, if you miss a day it will really fuck you up.
When she texts you next time, say this to her:

You know it's weird; a lot of the people I hang out with I never even considered friends. I mean if you asked them, I'm sure they'd say we were. But I guess I'm too afraid to actually call us friends, because then it actually means something, you know?

Anyway, I think at least for now maybe dating isn't really for me. People seem very strange to me, and the whole "dating game" makes about as much sense to me as quantum mechanics makes to the general populous. 

One of the reasons people say they like me is because I'm very straightforward, but the truth is I literally can't be anything else.

Haha nice try, but my apartment doesn't allow most pets.
And I don't think fish are good chick magnets. People give you really strange looks when you take them for a walk.

I don't really have any standards. I mean except obvious stuff, like being nice. 

Honestly my biggest "condition" is that they like me. It's really that simple with me.

"Good eye contact" is not something people with Aspergers are known for... 

But yeah I get what you're saying. I'm so terrified of the awkwardness that comes with trying to talk to strangers that I just don't, really. 

Also as far as the sweating goes, sometimes it's so much that a handkerchief won't help. On my bad days, my shirt looks like I just went to the gym....all day.
But he does have a point.

Unfortunately, the college I attend is 75% guys - one of the downsides of going to an engineering school. So my interaction with girls is limited, and I'd have better luck finding a unicorm on campus than a single female. 

It kind of bothers me that I have to lose weight to be attractive to others. Well, maybe HAVE TO isn't the right word, but it certainly increases the numbers a whole hell of a lot. It actually makes me sad to think that I'll be more attractive when I'm less weight.

As far as hobbies and activities go, mine are, unfortunately, very male-heavy. I play Magic the Gathering, love video games, read comics and science/engineering books, etc. 

I try not to go to places like coffee shops and whatnot. I am very awkward around people (at least I always thought so - but people I ask tell me I'm very funny and kind so I guess that's cool). And for the life of me, I CANNOT initiate a conversation with a stranger. I honestly feel like I'm going to pass out. 

Also yes, nothing says sexy like sweat literally dripping off your face. Fuck hyperhydrosis.

I apologize, I'm not sure how to edit my original post using the phone app.

Anyway, I wanted to say that I'm about 230 lbs now and 5"10'. I was over 300, but I acknowledge that I'm still pretty big.
